symptom: A microflow retrieve constraint written as an MDL STRING with the enum value quoted was stored truncated, with the following clause GONE: `WHERE 'Status = ''Mod.Status.Confirmed'' and Kind = Mod.Kind.Addition'` described back as `where Status = Mod.Status.;`. The retrieve returned rows it should have filtered out. `mxcli check` passed; only `mx check` caught it, as a generic CE0161 that does not say which clause (ako/CapTrackV3 FINDINGS §29).
cause: normalizeXPathEnumRefs ran its `Module.Enum.Value` regex over the WHOLE constraint with no quote awareness, so a ref the author had ALREADY quoted was rewritten inside its own quotes: `'Mod.Status.Confirmed'` -> `''Confirmed''`. Every downstream reader lexes `''` as an empty string literal, so re-parsing stopped at `Status = ''` and ANTLR error recovery swallowed the stray word, the second `''` and the entire ` and Kind = ...` tail; the describe enricher then rendered the empty value as `Mod.Status.`. Fixed by walking the constraint and running the regex only outside string literals — the same quote-skip NormalizeXPathOperators, FlattenXPathConstraint and stripMDLComments already use. Also fixed enumStringToQN double-qualifying an already-qualified stored value (`Xp.Status.Xp.Status.Confirmed`), which a describe -> exec would have written back.
insight: The reported case was not the whole bug. The same regex corrupted ANY XPath string literal containing two dots — `Code = 'a.b.c'` was stored as `Code = ''c''`, a constraint matching different rows, which nobody had noticed because it produces no build error at all. A string-level rewrite with no lexer is the recurring shape here; this repo already has three quote-aware scanners and the fourth site simply did not use one. The fix deliberately does NOT unquote the ref for the author: telling `'Mod.Status.Confirmed'` from `'a.b.c'` needs the project's enumerations, which that pass does not have, so the quoted spelling is stored verbatim and still fails as CE0161 — on a constraint that says what was written. A check rule that resolves the enum with -p is the remaining half and is not shipped here; a shape-only regex would false-positive on any dotted filename.
